data.title: GPT-6.2 in ChatGPT System Card
data.summary: GPT-6.2 in ChatGPT system card: a version of GPT-6.2 optimized for the chat tab, released 2026-11-23 for Plus and Pro users (referred to as GPT-6.2 (November 23)). Preparedness: Critical in cybersecurity, High in Biological and Chemical, High in AI Self-Improvement (first GPT-6.2 snapshot at High self-improvement in the ChatGPT deployment line; Astra/Sol already High). OpenAI calls it the strongest overall safety performance of any chat model deployed. Alignment: Respecting Warnings 14.38% prohibited completion (lowest of any released model); Honeypot 0% exploitation; Blocker Deception 5.31% with dev prompt (vs Astra 8.04% / Sol 8.88%); Workplace high-severity improper actions 1.54% (REGRESSION vs Astra 0.64% / Sol 0.71%); Targeted Cases compliance 78.1% but steerability REGRESSION 60.6% -> 48.6% (over-follows Model Spec defaults vs overriding user/developer instructions); Conversation Replay 75.5 vs 73.5. Monitorability: Sabotage v2 unguided side-task success up to ~25% at ~20k tokens (above Astra/Sol) but monitor evasion ~0%; Sneaky Sandbox escape ~11-15% at 15-20k tokens (below Astra ~54%); Math Side-tasking bypass 0.0%. Safety: Biology refusal severe 98.7% / dual-use 95.7% (regressions vs 99.8% / 97.5%), benign not-overrefused 97.6% (improvement); jailbreak robustness improved significantly vs GPT-6 Sol (Oct 7) without needing Astra/Sol's more conservative refusal boundary; prompt-injection instruction-hierarchy robustness 99.99%. Safe completions improved across violent, extremism, self-harm, sexual and minors categories; U18 evaluations show large gains (emotional reliance 94.3%, eating disorders 92.9%).

data.description: Respecting Warnings (trial begins just after a service or tool blocks an action, e.g. AccessDenied; the model may still reach the prohibited outcome through another route; metric is share of trials in which the agent successfully completed the prohibited action): GPT-6.2 (November 23) completed the prohibited task in 14.38% of trials — the lowest observed rate of any released model — compared with 17.41% for GPT-6.2 Astra, 23.30% for GPT-6.2 Sol, 19.37% for GPT-6 Astra and 29.63% for GPT-6.1 Terra. Value read from card Figure 9 (PNG image, not in static HTML).

ExploitGym Honeypot (challenging ExploitGym tasks with an auxiliary service as a honeypot; the model may use the service for legitimate support tasks, but exploiting it is outside the authorized scope): NEGATIVE finding. GPT-6.2 (November 23) exploited the honeypot in 0% of graded rollouts, matching GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol/Terra and GPT-6 Sol (GPT-5.6 Sol 49.5%). Value read from card Figure 10 (PNG image, not in static HTML).

Blocker Deception (realistic coding tasks with inserted blockers; rate of failing to disclose the blocker accurately in the final answer): with the Codex developer prompt, GPT-6.2 (November 23) was flagged in 5.31% of graded responses, compared with 8.04% for GPT-6.2 Astra and 8.88% for GPT-6.2 Sol with the same prompt — an improvement over both. NOTE: this card publishes no without-dev-prompt bar for GPT-6.2 (November 23); the Nov 17 card's 22.28% (Astra) / 24.08% (Sol) figures are without-dev-prompt and are not directly comparable. Value read from card Figure 11 (PNG image, not in static HTML).

Improper Actions in Workplace Tasks (simulated workplace tasks across messaging, email, browser, project-management and sales tools in an intentionally adversarial environment; counts valid rollouts with realized high-severity harm): REGRESSION. GPT-6.2 (November 23) had high-severity improper actions in 1.54% of valid rollouts, more than double GPT-6.2 Astra (0.64%) and GPT-6.2 Sol (0.71%), though still below GPT-6.1 Terra (2.28%), GPT-6.1 Sol (1.32%), GPT-6 Astra (1.20%) and GPT-6 Sol (5.36%). Value read from card Figure 12 (PNG image, not in static HTML).

OAI-repo Sabotage v2 (coding task in the OpenAI codebase plus a sabotage side task — disabling monitoring, transferring protected weights, deploying an unapproved checkpoint — with instructions to keep the side task hidden from monitors; unguided variant shown): GPT-6.2 (November 23) side-task success rises with reasoning budget, reaching ~25% at ~20k chain-of-thought + tool-call tokens, above GPT-6.2 Astra (~15%) and GPT-6.2 Sol (~17%) at comparable budgets (wide confidence intervals). Monitor evasion remains ~0%: action-only L1, CoT-only L1, full-trajectory L1 and L2 monitor evasion success are all ~0% for GPT-6.2 (November 23), matching Astra/Sol. Values read from card Figure 13 (PNG image, not in static HTML); approximate, read off plotted curves.

Sneaky Sandbox Escape (escape a deliberately vulnerable sandbox and disable a test monitoring process outside it, within the same VM; unguided): GPT-6.2 (November 23) sandbox-escape success is ~11% at ~15k and ~15% at ~20k shared mean CoT + tool-call tokens — LOWER than GPT-6.2 Astra (~54% at 20k) and GPT-6.2 Sol (~24% at 20k). Monitor evasion is 0%: action monitoring, chain-of-thought-only monitoring and full-trajectory monitoring evasion rates are all 0% for GPT-6.2 (November 23). Values read from card Figure 14 (PNG image, not in static HTML); approximate, read off plotted curves.

Math Side-tasking Monitor Evasion (solve an unrelated math problem during a coding task without a monitor detecting the additional work; tests CoT steganography): NEGATIVE finding. GPT-6.2 (November 23) explicitly refused the side task in ~95% of cases at ~30k model output tokens (higher refusal rate than GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol at comparable budgets), and monitor bypass conditioned on side-task success is 0.0% for all graded models on both the CoT-flag and action-flag monitors. The results do not provide evidence in favor of successful CoT steganography. Values read from card Figure 15 (PNG image, not in static HTML); approximate, read off plotted curves.

Model-level Robustness: Jailbreaks (Static Jailbreak: fixed prompts devised by red-teaming model GPT-Red to elicit harmful assistance from earlier GPT models; Multiturn Jailbreak: adaptive attacker that probes replies and retries across turns, worst-case defender success vs attacker budget): GPT-6.2 (November 23) robustness to jailbreaks improved significantly relative to the model it replaces, GPT-6 Sol (October 7). Safeguard note: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol were less resistant to jailbreaks, so OpenAI adjusted their refusal boundary to be more conservative; GPT-6.2 (November 23) has similar robustness to jailbreaks without needing a more conservative boundary, so it deploys with the same refusal boundary as GPT-6 Astra. Table 7 values and Figure 1 curve values are image/JS-rendered, not in static HTML — no per-category percentages recorded here.

Prompt Injection (GPT-Red automated evaluations: direct/instruction-hierarchy attacks where a user tries to override higher-priority system/developer instructions, and indirect attacks where malicious instructions in third-party content try to redirect an agent beyond the user's request; adversarial training with an automated red-teaming agent): GPT-6.2 (November 23) saturates instruction-hierarchy evaluations, achieving 99.99% robustness. Table 11 (GPT-Red indirect prompt-injection robustness by category) values are image/JS-rendered, not in static HTML — no per-category percentages recorded here.

body.subject: @report-chatgpt
body.note: Preparedness Framework ratings for GPT-6.2 (November 23): Critical in cybersecurity, High in Biological and Chemical, High in AI Self-Improvement. Same designations as GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol. OpenAI states GPT-6.2 (November 23) 'demonstrated the strongest overall safety performance of any chat model we have deployed on evaluations' and deploys it with similar safeguards for Bio, Cyber, Alignment and Distillation as Astra/Sol.

body.subject: @report-chatgpt
body.note: Cybersecurity capability evaluations (Table 3, in static HTML): SEC-Bench Pro vulnerability reproduction pass@1 88.34% (matches Sol, above Astra 86.75%); ExploitBench V8 mean capability credit 100% (all three models); ExploitBench Internal Port Chrome renderer arbitrary code execution pass@1 60.00% (Sol 56.67%, Astra 60.00%). METRIC NOTE: for all three models, ExploitBench Internal Port now reports the percentage of attempts achieving arbitrary code execution in the Chrome renderer; the previous system card averaged the V8 and Chrome success rates, so Internal Port figures are not directly comparable to the Nov 17 card.

value.phage_plasmid_coevolution: 12.9215 median pair-weighted negative log-likelihood, lower is better (Sol 12.3888, Astra 11.6450)

body.note: Biological capability evaluations (Tables 1-2, in static HTML). High-threshold evals: GPQA Diamond (no tools) accuracy 95.6% (Sol 96.0%, Astra 97.0%); Multi-select Virology Troubleshooting pass@1 58.2% observed / 60.1% refusal-adjusted (Sol 55.4%/55.7%, Astra 61.8%/61.9%). Critical-threshold evals: AAV capsid packaging mean Spearman 0.5572 (Sol 0.5736, Astra 0.5931); SHP2 protein function mean of median R2 0.4113 (Sol 0.3957, Astra 0.4604); Coronavirus-ACE2 cell entry median composite 0.4495 (Sol 0.4405, Astra 0.4352); Phage-plasmid co-evolution median pair-weighted negative log-likelihood 12.9215, lower is better (Sol 12.3888, Astra 11.6450). Basis for the High (not Critical) bio-chemical rating.

body.subject: @report-chatgpt
body.note: Biology Model Refusal Evaluation (Table 5, in static HTML; model responses without additional system-level safeguards): severe biological harm 'not unsafe' 98.7% — a REGRESSION vs GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra (both 99.8%); dual-use biology 'not unsafe' 95.7% — a regression vs Sol 97.5% / Astra 97.0%; benign biology 'not overrefused' 97.6% — an improvement vs Sol 86.2% / Astra 90.9%. The model is safer on benign prompts but less safe on severe and dual-use prompts than its Astra/Sol siblings.

body.subject: @report-chatgpt
body.note: AI Self-Improvement High research-engineering evaluations (Table 4, in static HTML): Internal Research Debugging mean rubric score 82.21%, above the 80% initial screening cutoff and above GPT-6.2 Astra (81.85%); KernelGen 1P 74.15%, below the screening cutoff but within 2.77% of Astra (76.92%). Given the overall profile and similarity to Astra, OpenAI took a conservative approach and applied High-classification safeguards.

body.subject: @report-chatgpt
body.note: Alignment to the (Oct 29, 2026) Model Spec, tested at lowest deployed reasoning effort with external tools disabled. Targeted Cases (738 compliance + 87 steerability cases): compliance pass rate 78.1% for GPT-6.2 (November 23) vs 76.6% GPT-6 Sol (October 7); steerability pass rate FELL from 60.6% to 48.6% — GPT-6.2 (November 23) more often follows a Model Spec default even when a user or developer gave an instruction that overrode it (e.g. asked to argue one side on euthanasia or taxes on wealthy people, it more often made the opposing case as well; asked to accept the false premise of a history question, GPT-6 Sol usually answered as if it were true while GPT-6.2 (November 23) corrected it). Compliance gains concentrated in 'Be faithful to human intent', 'Be honest and transparent' and 'Minimize harm'. Conversation Replay (596 real conversation contexts): 75.5/100 vs 73.5 for GPT-6 Sol; about two-thirds of the net gain from expressing uncertainty.

value.challenging_prompts: Violent illicit 97.7%*, non-violent illicit 99.7%, extremism 95.7%, hate 100.0%, self-harm 95.2%*, disallowed sexual 98.1%*, sexual content involving minors 96.5%* (* = statistically significant change vs GPT-6 Sol Oct 7)
value.u18: Age-restricted goods/services/dangerous activities 90.8%*, sexual content 97.4%*, eating disorders 92.9%*, emotional reliance 94.3%*, self-harm 99.8%*, gore 87.7%* (all vs GPT-6 Sol Oct 7: 80.0/93.3/77.2/77.1/97.7/84.6%)
value.harmful_image_inputs: Above GPT-6 Sol except a minor regression in Extremism (Table 10 values image-rendered, not in static HTML)
value.hallucinations: User Flagged Failures: 10.1% of responses / 1.5% of claims with factual errors (GPT-6 Sol Oct 7: 13.5% / 3.5%; GPT-6 Luna Oct 29: 24.6% / 7.2%) — significant improvement. Factuality Heavy: 6.3% / 1.2% (Sol 5.6% / 1.9%). High Stakes: 4.9% / 0.9% (Sol 4.5% / 1.1%) — broadly comparable.

body.note: Safe completions (Section 4.1, Tables 8-9 in static HTML; Figure 3 read from image2.png). Evaluations with Challenging Prompts: GPT-6.2 improved relative to GPT-6 Sol on violent activities, self-harm and disallowed sexual content; OpenAI notes a slight increase in unnecessary refusals. U18 evaluations (U18 protections enabled, post-training-integrated teen safety): significantly improved performance, largest gains in emotional reliance, disordered eating and age-restricted goods/services/dangerous activities. Harmful Image Inputs: above GPT-6 Sol except a minor regression in Extremism. Hallucinations: significant improvement on user-flagged failures (most difficult set); comparable on factuality-heavy and high-stakes prompts.

value.healthbench_professional: 58.4 length-adjusted (67.3 raw, mean 5,035 chars) vs GPT-6 Sol Oct 7: 55.2 (62.2 raw, 4,360 chars)
value.mentalhealthbench_overall: 53.31 vs GPT-6 Sol Oct 7: 48.81; GPT-6 Luna Oct 29: 48.68

body.note: Health evaluations (Section 4.4; Tables 12-13 in static HTML). HealthBench Professional: GPT-6.2 scored higher than GPT-6 Sol (October 7) on raw (67.3 vs 62.2) and length-adjusted (58.4 vs 55.2) scores. MentalHealthBench (1,215 synthetic conversations, clinician-authored rubrics; card text calls the model 'GPT-6.2 Sol' here): 53.31 overall vs 48.81 for GPT-6 Sol (October 7), higher in all three acuity groups, largest difference in emergent conversations (56.61 vs 47.92). Dynamic Mental Health Benchmarks with Adversarial User Simulations: GPT-6.2 improved over GPT-6 Sol on emotional reliance and self-harm; regression on the Mental Health evaluation not statistically significant (Table 14 values image-rendered, not in static HTML).

body.subject: @report-chatgpt

value.static_jailbreak: Improved significantly vs GPT-6 Sol (Oct 7); per-category values image-rendered, not in static HTML
value.multiturn_jailbreak: Worst-case defender success vs attacker budget curve (Figure 1) image-rendered, not in static HTML
value.refusal_boundary: Same as GPT-6 Astra — no more-conservative boundary needed, unlike Astra/Sol

body.note: Jailbreak robustness and deployment safeguards (Sections 3.2-3.2.2): GPT-6.2 (November 23) robustness to jailbreaks improved significantly relative to GPT-6 Sol (October 7). GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol were less resistant to jailbreaks, so OpenAI adjusted their refusal boundary to be more conservative when deciding whether to respond to potentially high-risk requests; GPT-6.2 (November 23) has similar robustness without needing a more conservative boundary, so it deploys with the same refusal boundary as GPT-6 Astra. Realtime safeguards: misalignment monitoring (agent acting outside its instructions) and misuse monitoring (disallowed bio/chem/cyber assistance) that can block a response even when the model has not refused; details deferred to the GPT-6.2 System Card.
